A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AGO framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original AGO occupancy-prediction experiments, zero-shot and few-shot evaluations, and component ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds AGO evaluations under VEON's open-world setting, Occ3D-Waymo experiments, and a retrieval example.

M1.justification: The encoder architecture, noise-augmented grounding, modality adapter, training losses, and entropy-based inference rule remain unchanged. The added evaluations and baseline implementation explanations do not establish a change to AGO's procedure.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates occupancy prediction only on Occ3D-nuScenes. V2 adds closed-world and staged open-world evaluations on Occ3D-Waymo, substantially broadening the driving data and category coverage (Appendix B.4, Tables G-H). Figure C also adds an open-vocabulary streetlight retrieval example.

E2.justification: VEON, previously compared only in the closed-world benchmark, becomes a direct open-world comparator in new Table F. The existing POP-3D, SelfOcc, and GaussTR comparisons remain. The change from PoP3D to POP-3D is a naming correction, not a new baseline.

E3.justification: New Table F introduces VEON's 0/17, 9/8, and 13/4 seen/unseen settings, with ground-truth supervision for seen categories, extending the original pseudo-label-based evaluation design. The new Waymo open-world evaluation excludes GO. Section 4.1 also revises the reported nuScenes scene split from 600/150/150 to 700/150/150; this does not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Figure C supplies a streetlight retrieval case study with average prediction entropy before and after the modality adapter, 0.582 and 0.497. Existing training-paradigm, inference-rule, component, backbone, resolution, loss-function, and adapter-depth ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that each few-shot experiment is repeated five times and averaged. V2 adds no new seed disclosures, variability estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retrieval example's prediction entropy does not change statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing nuScenes benchmark and ablation values are retained. New Table F reports AGO versus VEON mIoU of 22.42 versus 15.16 at 9/8 and 25.90 versus 19.94 at 13/4. New Waymo results include 16.02 versus GaussTR's 13.97 closed-world mIoU and 12.81 versus 9.16 after few-shot tuning (Tables G-H). These are additional settings, not improvements over v1 under identical conditions. VEON's reported parameter count also changes from 406.4M to 678.1M.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation in Equations 1-9, including the losses and entropy-based selection rule, is unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive grounding, noise prompts, modality adaptation, and open-world prediction. The claimed 4.09 mIoU advantage on the closed-world nuScenes benchmark is unchanged; the additional experiments support existing claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.4 attributes POP-3D's lower reported score to the stricter Occ3D evaluation protocol. Appendix A.5 further explains the supervision underlying SelfOcc's zero unknown-class performance. Existing modality-conflict interpretations and future directions concerning temporal information and richer prompts remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability URL and baseline reproduction details in Appendices A.4-A.5: borrowed versus retrained scores, POP-3D's 200×200×16 retraining resolution, and the baselines' losses and supervision across stages. These clarify retained experiments without establishing configuration changes. AGO's existing hyperparameters, hardware, and pseudo-label processing instructions are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds six references: TQD-Track, PETR, DETR3D, UniOcc, RenderWorld, and AutoOcc. It also moves the VEON discussion after the statement that preceding methods lack open-world prediction, excluding VEON from that criticism. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammar, terminology, and notation edits, standardizes POP-3D's name, and adds appendix subsections explaining comparisons and new evaluations. The main narrative and section organization are largely preserved rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: V2 adds appendix Tables F-H and the retrieval Figure C within the existing visual format. V1's Table F and Figure C are retained as Table I and Figure D. Existing main figures, tables, and appendix plots remain visually stable apart from caption edits and modest reflow.

improvement.justification: V1's empirical support was confined to nuScenes and its own open-world protocol. V2 substantially strengthens that support through a second dataset and VEON's alternative evaluation setting (Tables F-H), addressing important limits in experimental scope. Baseline retraining explanations and the code-access statement also improve reproducibility. Although documentation of the new benchmarks remains brief, the broader validation and clearer comparison procedures provide a substantial overall quality gain.
